description.value: The study examined insula-based resting-state functional connectivity abnormalities in Parkinson’s disease and depression-related connectivity differences between depressed and non-depressed PD patients.

spans.text: To identify whether PD patients had lower insula functional connectivity, all PD subjects were first pooled together and compared with the NC group.
Comparison between the depressed and non-depressed PD patients were then made to demonstrate depression-related changes.

design.value: Two groups of PD patients, with and without depression, and a matched normal control group underwent resting-state BOLD fMRI. Seed-based functional connectivity from bilateral anterior and posterior insula ROIs was compared across groups using general linear models with age and sex as covariates.
